title: Localizations of the integers are fields or discrete valuation rings
statement: The ring $\mathbf Z$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] Dedekind domain (that is, a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one) with fraction field $\mathbf Q$. Its prime ideals are $(0)$ and the ideals $(p)$ generated by rational primes $p$. The localization $\mathbf Z_{(0)}$ is the field $\mathbf Q$, and for every nonzero prime ideal $(p)$ the localization $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local discrete valuation ring (that is, a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal; see [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]) with maximal ideal $(p)\mathbf Z_{(p)}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), implication (1) => (2), together with Definition Tag 034W and Lemma Tag 0AUQ (a PID is Dedekind); the description of prime ideals of $\mathbf Z$ and $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$ is the elementary PID calculation used in the same lemma. The characterization of a Noetherian one-dimensional local domain as a DVR is Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr).

proof.text: Euclidean division shows every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal, so $\mathbf Z$ is a PID and its fraction field is $\mathbf Q$. It is Noetherian because every ideal is principal. It is integrally closed: if $a/b\in\mathbf Q$ is in lowest terms with $b>0$ and satisfies a monic equation over $\mathbf Z$, multiplying by $b^n$ shows $b$ divides $a^n$; coprimality forces $b=1$, so $a/b\in\mathbf Z$. Thus $\mathbf Z$ is a Noetherian integrally closed domain.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 034W, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), implication (1) => (2), and Lemma Tag 0AUQ; the integrally-closed calculation is the standard reduced-fraction proof for Z

proof.text: A prime ideal of the PID $\mathbf Z$ is generated by a prime element. The zero ideal is prime because $\mathbf Z$ is a domain, and a nonzero prime element is, up to sign, a rational prime; hence the prime ideals are exactly $(0)$ and $(p)$ for rational primes $p$. Each $(p)$ is maximal because $\mathbf Z/(p)$ is a field, while $(0)\subsetneq(p)$, so $\mathbf Z$ has Krull dimension one. With step 1 this makes $\mathbf Z$ a Dedekind domain by Stacks Definition 034W and Lemmas 0AUQ and 034X.

source.place: The elementary PID calculation used with Algebra, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), together with the definition of a prime ideal

proof.text: At $(0)$ every nonzero integer is inverted, so the fraction construction gives $\mathbf Z_{(0)}=\mathbf Q$, a field. Fix a rational prime $p$ and let $W=\mathbf Z\setminus(p)$. The canonical map $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z_{(p)}=W^{-1}\mathbf Z$ is a localization at $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] (1), its prime ideals correspond exactly to primes of $\mathbf Z$ disjoint from $W$, namely $(0)$ and $(p)$; their extensions are $(0)$ and $p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is local with maximal ideal $p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, and the only strict prime inclusion is $(0)\subsetneq p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$. Step 1 makes $\mathbf Z$ a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], so its localization is a normal domain with the same fraction field by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 034X (lemma-characterize-Dedekind), localization description in (1) => (2), and Lemma Tag 00E3 for prime correspondence under localization

proof.text: For $p\neq0$, the ring $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is therefore a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. Its normal-domain property is recorded in step 3. Applying the one-dimensional normal-local DVR criterion [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] (the Stacks Algebra Lemma 00PD criterion) gives that $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ is a discrete valuation ring. Together with the $(0)$ calculation, this proves the statement.
